children: shares jumped 13% on Wednesday as Wall Street firms weighed in on the company's investor day, held the day prior.

“[Management] unveiled its FY29 targets: a revenue CAGR of 14%-21%, non-GAAP operating margins of 20%-22%, and FCF margins of 12%-15%,” RBC Capital Markets analyst Rishi Jaluria wrote in a note to clients. “The execution required to achieve these targets, alongside competitive CDN dynamics, keeps us in wait-and-see mode. Shares traded down ~5%, meaningfully lagging the roughly flat IGV, driven by the wide FY29 revenue target range, in our view. We raise our FY27E estimates on defensive CDN and increased security contribution.” Jaluria has a Sector Perform rating and $25 price target on Fastly.
D.A. Davidson analyst Rudy Kessinger had a similar take, but also highlighted the new AI products the company unveiled.

“Mgmt. is focused on delivering a unified platform & driving broader platform adoption across product suites beyond CDN, w/ Security adoption in particular being a key focus as demand for newer Bot Management & DDoS products, which are each growing 100%+ Y/Y, remains very robust,” Kessinger explained. “New CY29 targets were generally impressive in our view given FSLY's end markets and were ahead of cons. expectations, though slight implied decel vs. CY26 guidance was likely underwhelming for bulls w/ unrealistic AI expectations.” Kessinger kept his Neutral rating on Fastly but upped his price target to $23 from $21.
Piper Sandler analyst James Fish noted that the 2029 target range was "slightly above" the buyside expectations and said this could be conservative, given the rise of agentic AI.

“Fastly should continue to benefit near-term from the current market dynamics, but we have concerns that this can persist for ~3 years for where the company is primarily exposed to,” Fish explained. “Our estimates move slightly higher, and we are at the low-end of the '29 sales guide but high-end FCF.”

title: Fastly jumps as Wall Street weighs in on investor day
